chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Attar, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'We have delayed in receiving sustenance.' So he (peace be upon him) got angry, then said: 'Say.'

O Allah, You have guaranteed my sustenance and the sustenance of every animal. So, O the Best of the supplicated to, and O the Best of the ones asked from, and O the best of the ones who give, and O the Most Superior of the ones hoped from, Do for me such and such.

key_terms.دَابَّة: Animal/Beast (often used for all living creatures)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for delayed sustenance in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects the companion Abu Basir’s complaint of delayed sustenance by attributing it to a deficiency in supplication rather than divine neglect. He prescribes a specific du'a that emphasizes God's universal guarantee of rizq for all creatures, highlighting the Shia scholarly view that spiritual readiness and proper invocation are prerequisites for receiving blessings. This context underscores the importance of active spiritual engagement in the process of divine provision.
